broadcasts.subject: Friday Favorites
broadcasts.content:
Hi Meanies!

Happy Friday! From time to time I like to take stock of the things in my life that are especially fun and share them with you. Here's my short list for the week. I'd love to hear yours!

What I'm enjoying right now:
​​
​Bluey (kids TV show) - My family has been really enjoying this show on Disney+. It's about a family of Australian cattle dogs. These dogs are continuously a role model of fun, light-hearted, and connected parenting. My favorite episode so far is Bike, which is about failure and developing grit. It made me cry. If you have kids, I encourage you to dance to the intro music with them.

Stillwater (kids tv show) - This is a show about a family that lives next door to a panda on Apple TV. It teaches mindfulness and how to deal with big emotions — something that my family and I always need reminders of. It's slow paced and real.

Magic Spoon (fun cereal for adults) - My wife bought me a few boxes of this amazing cereal. I enjoy into eating well and healthy and love having a treat that fits in my fitness nutrition macros. Plus the branding and design is really fun. If kids cereals without the sugar sound interesting, this is for you. So far the "Fruity" flavor is my favorite. It tastes like Frootloops. Yummmm.

​Miroco Kettle (coffee/tea kettle) - My wife also bought me a new kettle for making coffee and tea at home. It's pretty, well balanced, and can hold your water at just the right temperature for whatever you're brewing. It makes me happy every time I use it — and I use it 2+ times a day!

​Simple exercise bands (fitness equipment) - This is fitness-geek-ish, but I bought a set of these to keep me working out while traveling, and have used them every day since. Life with small kids and multiple businesses leaves me short on time for workouts. These allow me to squeeze in some extra movements here and there between other activities. It's my current workout secret sauce.

What's on your Friday Favorites list? I'd love to know what you're enjoying in life right now!

-Dan

Through her work Laura helps people come to understand how others see them, take control of that narrative, and use it to their advantage.

This conversation was a blast. We talk about why "soft-skills" matter so much, how much fun footnotes are, and lots of other great things.

broadcasts.content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

Our guest today has had a fascinating career path. I could say that about all our guest, really. Who hasn't had a fascinating career path?

But that's some of what makes these conversations so important! It's rarely linear. It never looks the way you think it will.

But I digress.

When Ximena Vengoechea realized that the path she was on wasn't going to take her where she wanted to go, she started researching and exploring her curiosity around startups and tech. I love the process that she created for herself and where it took her.

I'll let her share that story and how you can apply a similar process to your work and any transition you may be considering.

Today Ximena is a user researcher, author, and illustrator. She's taken what she's learned about really listening and drawing out the essence of what someone is bringing into a conversation into her new book, Listen Like You Mean It — Reclaiming the Lost Art of True Connection.

In our conversation, we dig into her career journey, her current work, and some of the great takeaways from her new book. It's a blast. I think you'll really enjoy this one.

broadcasts.subject: How should I end this?
broadcasts.content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

It's the end of the year. This brings a valuable opportunity to reflect and reset.

And boy do we need it this year.

It’s tempting to flip the calendar to 2021 without thinking back about 2020, but it’s more important than ever not to move ahead to quickly.

If you're anything like me, I can hardly remember the start of 2020. It’s uniquely vague, unlike most years.

(Granted, my wife and I had a baby in the middle of the year, and combined with the other two kids we already had — I haven’t gotten as much sleep this year as I would have liked.)

My sleep and parenting struggles aside, 2020 is a year that has changed a lot for many people.

And it’s important to take note.

Many of us had work situations change in 2020.

Many of us had social situations change in 2020.

Many of us stayed home a lot in 2020.

Many of us had more time on our hands in 2020.

Many of us had less time on our hands in 2020.

Many of us lost a loved one in 2020.

Let’s not let these changes pass us by without reflection.

2021 may or may not bring about a better world — I hope it does! But no matter what, you won't won't be able to create a future that you want to create unless you understand where you've been.

As we change calendar years, there is tremendous value is doing two things: looking back and looking forward.

Some years ago I created an Annual Review guide to help with this process. It walks you through a process of pausing, reflecting, evaluating, and goal setting.

It’s free. I hope you’ll take some time to do it along with me.

​Click here to get it: https://themeaningmovement.com/annual-review/​

This year more than any other.

See you next year,

-Dan

Finding Meaning without a Job Change

broadcasts.content:
Hi Meanies,

I was just in your inbox with the first video in this 3 part masterclass. I'm LOVING the replies that I'm getting! Keep them coming!

But I'm visiting your inbox fagain, because I need to get real with you.

I remember feeling REALLY stuck. I didn’t know what to do with my life. I had been working a job for a long time that didn’t fit but I stayed in it because I thought it was what I was “supposed to do” based on my degree, disposition, gender, experience, and others’ expectations of me. All these things contributed to a mindset that kept me in this job far too long – eventually negatively impacting my mental and physical health, and my family life as well.

Deep down, if I really listened, I knew I needed to identify and find something different. But, I didn’t know what, or how, or if I was good enough. I was dominated by fear.

Fearful of putting all my effort into a business plan or job application that may not pan out.

Fearful of being told I was “asking too much” for my life.

Fearful of being judged by my friends and family.

Fearful of wanting a role that didn’t yet exist.

Fearful of letting people down.

Ultimately what I ended up fearing the most was this: things staying the same.

What would happen to my life if I stayed in this job? Would I be happy, or wake up years later a miserable human?

With that, I challenge you to begin this journey by naming your own fears. Take a moment and identify your fears and beliefs that hold you back from giving this aspect of your life the attention and consideration it deserves.

There are no right or wrong answers; only your truth. I'll read every response and do my best to keep up with replies.

Onward Meanies!
